section_summary: This section covers two strands of political change in occupied Japan: a progress report on national reforms and a detailed account of efforts to teach democratic local government. It also reports Tokyo's adoption of a public security ordinance governing demonstrations. Much of the section consists of a memorandum on a local autonomy conference at Uji-Yamada and the beginning of an accompanying instructional paper on citizenship.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Copy of “Brief Progress Report on Political Reorientation of Japan”
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a Government Section report on political reform in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The despatch outlines the report's account of constitutional and governmental reforms, then cautions that their permanence remains unproved and that the report understates Occupation influence.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Public Security Ordinance
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports passage and implementation of Tokyo's public security ordinance.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance requires advance notice for demonstrations; opposition and small clashes accompanied its passage.

subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Notice for Tokyo Despatch No. 738
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.about: Designates an attached copy of despatch no. 738 as the replacement record copy.
subfiles.summary: Requests return of the replacement copy for central filing.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Memorandum on “Local Autonomy Program for the Cities of Japan”
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits William L. Magistretti's memorandum on a local autonomy conference at Uji-Yamada.
subfiles.summary: Sebald summarizes Magistretti's view that democratic progress depends on civic education, economic recovery, and Japanese participation.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Memorandum on “Local Autonomy Program for the Cities of Japan”
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Provides an action copy of the same covering despatch and its assessment.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate covering despatch for Magistretti's memorandum on local autonomy and prospects for Japanese democracy.

subfiles.title: Local Autonomy Program for the Cities of Japan—Conference at City of Uji-Yamada
subfiles.from: William L. Magistretti, American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: Describes an Eighth Army civic education conference and assesses local democracy in Mie Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Magistretti describes the conference's prepared lectures and public discussions on mayors, assemblies, taxation, public services, recall, and women's participation. He records concern over inconsistent tax assessments, inadequate municipal revenue, lingering political habits, and local economic hardship. He concludes that democracy is gaining support but needs education, economic improvement, and sustained civic participation.

subfiles.title: The Citizen in Japan
subfiles.from: Legal and Government Division, Civil Affairs Section, Headquarters Eighth Army
subfiles.about: Explains citizens' responsibilities under Japan's Constitution and Local Autonomy Law.
subfiles.summary: This first paper in the local autonomy program draws on historical examples of cities to argue for popular sovereignty and local control of local affairs. It discusses citizenship, informed voting, candidate selection, taxation, lawful appeals, and civic involvement in municipal policy. The text continues beyond page 215.
